text.p: Advanced Tissue Sciences Inc said a panel of outside experts convened by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration recommended the agency approve its Dermagraft bioengineered skin replacement for use as temporary covering for severe burns.

It said the recommendation for approval was made with the condition that the company conduct post-marketing surveillance to generate additional information relative to infection rates. No specific requirements for the post-marketing surveillance were mandated, but the panel said the company should work with the FDA to develop a monitoring methodology.

The vote to recommend approval was made after the company presented pivotal clinical trial data demonstrating that Dermagraft-TC successfully reached its primary endpoint, the ability of the product to adequately prepare the burn wound bed for successful autografting, Advanced Tissue said.

Stndard wound management for third degree burn victims involves the excision of burned tissue and the temporary covering of the wound with cadaver skin (allograft), a step necessary to prevent infection and prepare the wound bed for eventual placement of autograft tissue (skin from an unburned portion of the patient's own body). Dermagraft-TC was designed to act as a temporary wound covering that, like cadaver allograft, would prevent fluid loss and promote a vascularized wound bed for autograft.
